newsitem.title: UK: P&O dips as Stena's losses mount.
newsitem.headline: P&O dips as Stena's losses mount.

text.p: Shares in Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co dipped on Wednesday after rival ferry operator Stena Line AB of Sweden reported widening losses in the first half, traders said.

However, analysts said P&O should not have been hit by Stena's results as the Swedish ferry operator blamed currency losses, and delays in new ferry deliveries, for contributing to its 560 million crowns loss in the first half.

The two lines compete on the English Channel, the world's busiest short-sea shipping lane, where they also face a strong competitive threat from Eurotunnel Plc/SA's channel tunnel. Stena lost 350 million crowns in the same period of 1995.
P&O's shares were trading at 519.5 p, down 4.0 pence, by 0845 GMT.
"Stena..is blaming its problems on late ferry deliveries and foreign currency losses not on difficulties on cross Channel routes," said Matthew O'Keefe, analyst at UBS.
Stena said that high season traffic across the Channel had been dominated by heavy price discounting, but O'Keefe said this was well known by the market.
